newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta's current account deficit falls in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Malta's current account deficit falls in Q2.

text.p: Malta's current account deficit fell by 19.8 million Maltese lire ($55.5 million) to Lm16.6 million in the second quarter from Lm36.4 million in the first, the Central Office of Statistics said on Monday.

The merchandise trade deficit fell by Lm15.2 million to Lm63.9 million in the same period as exports rose and imports fell. Net travel earnings declined by Lm2.2 million to Lm38.2 million while net investment income dropped by Lm3.0 million to Lm7.2 million in June.
The office noted a higher surplus in the unrequited transfers account, rising mainly from a grant from the Italian government.

It said net capital flows increased by Lm26.5 million as net outflows in the monetary sectors dropped by Lm21.7 million to Lm6.4 million. Net inflows in the non-monetary sectors rose by Lm4.9 million to Lm25.4 million in June.
The official reserves rose by Lm0.3 million in June compared to a drop of Lm32.6 million in the second quarter of 1995.
